newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Wooltru unit plans to up sales, outlets.
newsitem.headline: Wooltru unit plans to up sales, outlets.

text.p: South African retailer Dion, which is part of the listed Wooltru Ltd group, said on Tuesday it planned to double its sales and the number of outlets in the next three to four years.

The firm, which on Tuesday opened two new stores, bringing its total shops to 21, said it was confident the expansion would add more than 100 million rand a year to group turnover -- budgeted at 1.2 billion rand this year.

Managing director Dave McAlpin said in a statement that Dion, which was bought by Wooltru subsidiary Massmart in 1993, had started expanding again following a period of consolidation and the closure of stores in 1995.
"Management is delighted at the dramatic upturn in Dion's fortunes and is confident from now on the shareholders will receive a good return on their investment," McAlpin said.
He added that operating profit this year would be partially offset by a large investment in systems.
